# Research: Orca nested worker depth, helpers, and sub-coordinator roles

**Status:** Complete — research returned inline under the approved delivery adaptation  
**Date:** 2026-11-09  
**Scope:** Phase 4, Step 4.4, web-04 only  
**Parent output destination:** `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/.dev/tasks/to-do/TASK-RESEARCH-sub-orchestrator-mode-20261108-181115/research/web-04-orca-nested-depth-helpers.md`  
**Web search provenance:** `provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable`

## Summary

Public Orca sources explicitly support workers delegating to helper workers. A newer public release documents a default nesting depth of **four**, whereas the installed build’s source defaults to **one**, and the inspected stored profile field is also **one**. Neither observation establishes the effective setting currently loaded by the running application.

**Public sub-coordinator evidence was found, but not a separately defined role.** Public documentation mentions “nested coordinators,” and a public issue discusses workers acting as local coordinators. Neither establishes a distinct sub-coordinator role with its own authority, reporting, recovery, or permission contract.

This strengthens the case for evaluating native supervised helpers if IronClaude revisits its restriction. It does **not** authorize that use: current WC-13 prohibits worker-session Orca fan-out at any depth setting, and D5 retains explicit reconsideration gates.

## Method, discovery, and evidence boundaries

- First read the exact assigned task text at lines 282–284.
- Read research03, research06’s Summary and Key Takeaways, and the current gaps register.
- Inspected relevant installed package metadata fields only. The archive’s root `package.json` supplied the homepage `https://github.com/stablyai/orca`; the unpacked compiled-output metadata supplied the installed version.
- Followed repository links and search-discovered URLs to documentation, releases, issues, and pull requests. No URLs were constructed from guessed source paths.
- Tavily tools and aliases were absent from the available tool list. All external retrieval therefore used the permitted WebSearch/WebFetch fallback.
- Retrieved the installed version-matched CLI and orchestration guides with read-only `skills get` calls, then located and read relevant bundled guide source.
- Used no Write, Edit, Agent, Task, Team, SendMessage, GitHub CLI, authentication, or Orca mutation operations. No tests, launches, setting changes, or live nesting experiments ran.
- Excluded unrelated products named Orca. External queries contained public Orca identifiers and generic topic terms, not private code or private issue text.

## Finding 1 — Package metadata identifies the correct public project

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for package identity and the public landing page  
**Relationship:** Supports reliable discovery; prevents confusion with other Orca products  
**Sources:** [Public repository](https://github.com/stablyai/orca), [installed metadata](file:///opt/Orca/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/package.json)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The installed archive’s root package metadata identifies its homepage as `https://github.com/stablyai/orca`. The public repository page identifies Orca as a multi-agent coding interface and links to [the orchestration documentation](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration).

[CODE-VERIFIED] Installed compiled-output metadata reports version **`1.4.245-aidev02.780594c521aa`** and commit **`780594c521aaa2399b242b0022045017f4a77436`** at L1:5–6. That metadata contains no homepage, repository, or documentation field; the root archive homepage supplied the discovery link.

The public repository landing page labels the repository public and describes it as open source. That does not prove every implementation URL is accessible: the search-discovered [preamble source URL](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/src/main/runtime/orchestration/preamble.ts) returned HTTP 404 during direct retrieval.

## Finding 2 — Default one was not an enduring public product decision

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for maintainer-stated rationale and merged-change history; MEDIUM for reported runtime behavior  
**Relationship:** Extends research03; challenges treating depth one as Orca’s permanent architectural recommendation  
**Sources:** [Original depth PR #16668](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/16668), [default-change PR #38348](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The original PR describes an accidental restriction arising from workers lacking the Run attachment required by worker startup. It introduced caller-dispatch-based depth accounting, retaining default one.

The later PR states that one had not been deliberately selected as the desired product default. It raises the default to four and explains that a ceiling remains to prevent runaway recursive delegation. **No rationale for choosing exactly four rather than another finite number was found in the retrieved PR.**

[CODE-VERIFIED] The installed implementation still defines default one and root depth zero, rejects unsafe/noninteger values below one by falling back to one, and tells a refused worker to finish locally (L2:6–26). Its comment explicitly connects that instruction to avoiding repeated attempts at unavailable dispatch.

These are different-version facts, not grounds to substitute the public default for the installed default.

## Finding 3 — Public release v1.4.251 changes the default and migrates stored ones

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for published release and migration statements; MEDIUM for behavior not independently executed  
**Relationship:** Extends the version-risk analysis and contradicts applying current public default four to this installed build  
**Sources:** [v1.4.251 release](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.251), [PR #38348](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [official documentation](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration), [release listing](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

| Surface | Observed statement |
|---|---|
| Installed source | [CODE-VERIFIED] Default `1` — L2 |
| Inspected stored profile | [CODE-VERIFIED stored data] `settings.nestedWorkerMaxDepth = 1` — L9 |
| Effective running setting | [UNVERIFIED] Not established by either source default or stored JSON |
| Public v1.4.251 | Default `4`; release entry displayed “06 Nov 06:31” |
| Public release listing | Displayed v1.4.255 as latest at retrieval |
| Public documentation | Default `4`; previous stored ones migrate once; later choices are retained |
| Documentation version | No explicit documentation build/version was displayed |

The PR describes these migration cases:

- An unmarked stored one becomes four once.
- Values above one remain unchanged.
- A subsequent explicit selection of one remains one.
- Previously intentional ones cannot be distinguished from persisted defaults, so an **unmarked intentional one also migrates**.

**Decision implication:** an upgrade requires explicit policy review. It could widen native runtime capability without changing IronClaude’s worker contract. No upgrade or setting change is recommended or authorized by this investigation.

## Finding 4 — Native helpers already have a parent-worker recipe

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for installed source and guide text; MEDIUM for public author-reported execution  
**Relationship:** Supports research03’s native-helper direction; corrects historical assumptions that every helper report must reach the root coordinator  
**Sources:** [PR #38348](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [public guide](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/skill-guides/orchestration.md), [installed bundle](file:///opt/Orca/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/main/chunks/orcad-migration-source-retention-B_-OYaBD.js)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The public PR says eligible workers receive an existing helper-instruction section; it does not present helper delegation as a newly invented role.

[CODE-VERIFIED] The installed preamble includes its `SUB-DISPATCH` section conditionally. The ordinary local section:

- Places helpers in the parent worker’s Dispatch Run.
- Specifies `worker-start --from` with the worker handle.
- Says helper questions, escalations, and completion messages arrive in the worker’s own `check`, alongside its coordinator’s messages.
- Requires waiting for every helper’s completion before reporting the parent’s own completion.

Evidence: L3:460 and 493–505. The preamble also contains a distinct own-Run variant at L3:509–519; it must not be conflated with the local same-Run recipe.

[CODE-VERIFIED] At L3:640, `$et` offers helper instructions when dispatch depth is below the runtime maximum. The `iJ` recipient selector chooses an active same-Run creator Dispatch when available, otherwise the owning Run. Local helper validation rejects `--on` and `--terminal` for that route.

[UNVERIFIED] This inspection did not prove successful live startup, delivery, reply, restart, or recovery. It verifies source mechanisms, not a completed local nested run.

## Finding 5 — Public “nested coordinators” exist as wording, not a complete role contract

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for the actual documentation wording; MEDIUM for functional needs reported in an issue  
**Relationship:** Extends the role discussion while rejecting a stronger claim of an already-defined sub-coordinator role  
**Sources:** [Public CLI documentation source](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/site/content/docs/cli/orchestration.mdx), [delegation request #24970](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/24970), [installed guide](file:///opt/Orca/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/bundled-skill-guides.js)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The public documentation describes group messages reaching Dispatch mailboxes or child-Run mailboxes for **“nested coordinators.”** This is messaging behavior, not a definition of how such a coordinator obtains authority or supervises its children.

Issue #24970 supplies a functional example: workers assigned phases should launch reviewers or implementation helpers without routing every launch through the primary coordinator. A commenter describes selected workers acting as local coordinators for reusable workflows.

[CODE-VERIFIED text] The installed role table lists exactly:

1. Coordinator.
2. Dispatched worker.
3. Handoff owner.
4. Compatibility operator.
5. Ordinary terminal agent.

It contains no separate sub-coordinator row (L4:2372–2380). Installed CLI wording also mentions nested coordinators’ child-Run mailboxes (L5:76).

**Explicit answer:** Public nested-coordinator terminology and functional local-coordinator requests were found. **A separately defined public sub-coordinator role with a complete authority and lifecycle contract was not found in the inspected material.** This is bounded negative evidence, not proof that no such definition exists anywhere.

## Finding 6 — Public demand supports the use case, not a measured benefit

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** MEDIUM — first-hand reports and requests, not controlled measurements  
**Relationship:** Supports the proposed value while leaving D5’s local evidence gate open  
**Sources:** [Issue #24970](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/24970), [remote-depth issue #30141](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/30141)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

Public reports describe two relevant needs:

- Let a phase worker start its own reviewers or implementation helpers.
- Let a remote lead worker delegate smaller tasks without returning every launch to the desktop coordinator.

These support **plausible value**: local decomposition and fewer coordinator-mediated launches. They do not establish quantified latency savings, lower token use, better correctness, or a qualifying IronClaude runtime-discovered split.

[CODE-VERIFIED decision text] D5 requires both a defined composite brief and a real run recording a runtime-only split whose extra round trip was material; it also requires the specified trace before any raise (L7:405). Public requests do not satisfy those project-specific conditions.

## Finding 7 — Remote host depth remains a separate concern

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** MEDIUM for reported remote behavior; HIGH for the PR’s stated boundaries  
**Relationship:** Supports retaining research03’s federation uncertainty instead of generalizing local helper results  
**Sources:** [Issue #30141](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/30141), [PR #38348](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The remote issue reports that raising the desktop allowance did not change a remote host’s default one. It asks for owner-controlled remote configuration that workers cannot use to increase their own allowance.

The default-change PR says hosts enforce their own limits and older hosts retain their previous behavior until updated. **Closure of the issue does not establish that the requested privileged remote-configuration mechanism was implemented.**

[UNVERIFIED locally] This research did not establish remote effective settings, cross-host propagation, remote helper recovery, or a supported per-Run override. Local same-Run helper source does not close those gaps.

## Finding 8 — Newer public helper shutdown behavior must not be backported by assumption

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for release statements; MEDIUM for detailed author-reported behavior  
**Relationship:** Extends failure analysis; does not verify this installed build’s cleanup guarantees  
**Sources:** [v1.4.251 release](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.251), [helper-stop PR #38373](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38373)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

The release announces that stopping a worker stops its helpers. The linked PR describes following creator-Dispatch descendants rather than stopping every agent sharing a workspace.

Its detailed account includes important qualifications:

- Preserved helpers and their descendants can remain active.
- Unconfirmed shutdown remains uncertain.
- Remote shutdown requires contact with the relevant host.
- Interrupted initialization can require another shutdown request.
- Closing terminals is not a universal guarantee that detached processes died.

[UNVERIFIED locally] No equivalent complete shutdown/recovery guarantee was established for the installed `1.4.245-aidev02` build. The public release statement is therefore not evidence that parent termination safely settles every descendant here.

## Finding 9 — Native capability does not amend IronClaude’s contract

**Relevance:** HIGH  
**Reliability:** HIGH for directly read local instruction text  
**Relationship:** Contradicts interpreting public helper support or general ownership wording as current permission  
**Sources:** [Public helper change](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [current worker contract](file:///home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md), [ownership wording](file:///home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/src/superclaude/core/CLAUDE.md)

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

[CODE-VERIFIED instruction text] WC-13 prohibits worker-session calls to worker startup, dispatch, task creation, and general Orca agent/worktree launches **at any depth setting** (L6:62). The coordinator section describes a session opened by the person (L6:69).

[CODE-VERIFIED instruction text] General ownership wording recognizes “a coordinator under another orchestrator,” but the immediately preceding wording preserves the supervised worker contract (L8:55–59).

[CODE-CONTRADICTED if asserted as current permission] Neither public depth four nor the ownership phrase authorizes supervised middle-layer fan-out in IronClaude today.

| Public default applied locally | [CODE-CONTRADICTED] Public default four cannot describe the installed source default one |
| Local depth-two lifecycle | [UNVERIFIED] Startup, questions/replies, simultaneous parent/helper mail, settlement, restart, and recovery were not exercised |
| Historical root-mailbox prediction | [CODE-CONTRADICTED for ordinary local helpers] Installed preamble and creator-recipient selector provide the parent-worker route; universal routing guarantees still require broader/live verification |
| Separate public sub-coordinator role | [UNVERIFIED] Wording and functional requests exist, but no complete role contract was found |
| Why exactly four | [UNVERIFIED] Retrieved rationale explains finite limiting, not the chosen number |
| Quantified local benefit | [UNVERIFIED] Public requests and author tests do not satisfy D5’s measured IronClaude trigger |

| Remote configuration and per-Run override | [UNVERIFIED] Issue closure does not prove an owner-only remote setter or supported per-Run setting |
| Newer shutdown guarantees on this installation | [UNVERIFIED] Do not assume v1.4.251 behavior is present or complete here |
| Depth cap as a safety boundary | [UNVERIFIED if asserted universally] A depth limit alone does not establish total-worker, permission, spending, or process-isolation guarantees |
| Agent-tool limits and hook installation | [UNVERIFIED] This Orca-focused public research does not settle provider/adapter limits or local hook installation questions |
| Inaccessible public implementation path | [UNVERIFIED] Its reason for returning 404 is unknown; no private source access was attempted |
| Permission to use helpers now | [CODE-CONTRADICTED] WC-13 still prohibits it; neither native support nor a role label changes that |

## Key External Findings

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

- **HIGH relevance; HIGH reliability:** Public Orca moved its default from one to four and described one as an accidental carryover, not its permanent desired architecture. [PR #38348](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348)
- **HIGH relevance; HIGH reliability:** v1.4.251 documents the default change and one-time migration. Installed source and stored data remain separate facts. [Release](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.251)
- **HIGH relevance; HIGH reliability:** Public documentation explicitly mentions nested coordinators, but that sentence concerns mailbox routing, not a complete sub-coordinator role. [Documentation source](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/site/content/docs/cli/orchestration.mdx)
- **HIGH relevance; MEDIUM reliability:** Public requests support phase-local delegation and remote lead-worker helpers; they provide no measured IronClaude benefit. [#24970](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/24970), [#30141](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/30141)
- **HIGH relevance; HIGH/MEDIUM reliability:** Helper shutdown is important enough to have a separate public change with explicit uncertainty and recovery caveats. [PR #38373](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38373)
- **HIGH relevance; HIGH reliability for installed source:** The installed helper preamble and creator-mailbox selector support research03’s native-helper finding, while the current local contract still prohibits its use. [Installed bundle](file:///opt/Orca/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/main/chunks/orcad-migration-source-retention-B_-OYaBD.js), [worker contract](file:///home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md)

## Recommendations from External Research

<!-- web-provenance: provider=WebSearch reason=tavily-unavailable -->

1. **Retain O1 with O6’s explicit reconsideration gates now.** Public capability removes an argument that nesting is inherently unsupported; it does not supply the missing local permission, measured need, or lifecycle evidence. [Public capability](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [current D5](file:///home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/.dev/orca-command-refactor/specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md)

2. **If the decision is reopened, evaluate O3 native supervised helpers before treating O4 handoff ownership as equivalent.** The installed native path already supplies a parent-worker recipe and recipient selection. A handoff role is explicitly different in the installed guide and does not establish an upward supervision contract. [Public delegation need](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/24970), [installed role and helper guide](file:///opt/Orca/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/bundled-skill-guides.js)

3. **Keep native capability, IronClaude authority, workspace ownership, and role terminology separate in the decision report.** “Nested coordinator” wording is evidence of a supported concept, not a grant of transitive permissions. [Public routing wording](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/site/content/docs/cli/orchestration.mdx), [WC-13](file:///home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/fix-flaky-parallel-thread-test/src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md)

4. **Treat version and migration review as a prerequisite to any future authorized evaluation.** Record each host’s installed build, effective setting, and migration behavior; do not assume desktop settings govern remote workers or that an older intentional one survives migration unchanged. [Migration PR](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [remote request](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/30141)

5. **Require explicit lifecycle and resource limits before endorsing a sub-mode.** The decision must address helper count, write scope, result admission, parent/helper mailbox handling, cancellation, orphan recovery, and retained descendants. Public finite depth and shutdown claims do not settle those project obligations. [Depth rationale](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348), [shutdown qualifications](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38373)

Complete — web-04 research returned inline for parent persistence; no files or runtime state changed, and live nesting, effective settings, private implementation, and recovery behavior remain untested.
